newsitem.title: UK: TEPCO doubts Japan nuclear power goal realistic.
newsitem.headline: TEPCO doubts Japan nuclear power goal realistic.

text.p: An official at Japan's biggest electricity utility Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc on Thursday expressed doubt about government targets to raise nuclear output to 42 percent of electricity production by 2010.

"I'm not sure if government plans will happen in reality or not...There may be some difficulties to be overcome by companies but we will try," TEPCO managing director Tokio Kanoh told Reuters in an interview while attending a conference here.
Japan aims to raise the share of nuclear power from 33 percent to 42 percent by 2010, with capacity rising from 40 to 70 gigawatts.
Kanoh also dismissed a recent "no" vote for nuclear power in the northern town of Maki as a "special case," and said TEPCO would push ahead with plans to increase its reliance on nuclear power.
In a referendum last month, residents of Maki voted against building a new nuclear station planned by Tohoku Electric Power Co, although the vote is not legally binding.
"It is a local matter for the Maki people. Maki is a special case," Kanoh said. "If you see another place like Kushima... local people are welcoming another construction of nuclear power."
TEPCO was already building two more nuclear plants to add to its current 15 sites, and planned to build more, he added.
Kanoh said he was confident about the safety of TEPCO's latest advanced boiling water reactor design, which experienced a glitch during trial operation earlier this year.
Looking to the future, Kanoh said fast breeder reactors, the next generation of reactor which run on plutonium, were an indispensible option for the 21st century.
